playbooks.description: Opens the BottomNav@1.2.0 preview harness (example=mobile-primary) at top level, focuses the first navigation item, presses Tab, and asserts focus advances to a later item that is still inside the nav element. Proves BottomNav items are keyboard-reachable in sequence rather than only pointer-operable.

Drives the real adopted Dialog component (react-component-library:Dialog@1.1.0) as used live on the Adoptions page. Opens the create-adoption dialog via its trigger, confirms the role=dialog surface mounts, presses Escape, and asserts the dialog unmounts. Proves the Dialog's Escape-to-close contract behaviorally, not just that it renders.

Opens the DrawerShell@1.0.0 preview harness (example=full-open) at top level and proves the focus trap: after focusing the in-panel close button and pressing Tab, keyboard focus stays inside the role=dialog panel instead of leaking to the backdrop or document body. This is the exact failure class the DrawerShell pilot exposed that screenshot-diffs cannot catch. The paired calibration bas/calibration/drawershell-focus-trap-broken.json runs the same assertion against DrawerShell@0.1.0 (which has no useFocusTrap) and must fail.

Opens the Select@1.1.0 preview harness (example=selected, defaultValue=native) at top level, focuses the combobox, presses ArrowDown, and asserts the selected value advances from 'native' to 'compatible'. Proves the Select component honours keyboard option navigation, not merely that it renders a combobox.

Navigates to the seeded StatusBadge component editor at desktop width (where the code+preview panels render side by side) and asserts the preview host reaches the Rendered badge. This fails when the iframe recursively loads the app shell or when the preview runtime reports a browser render error. The mobile-only Preview/Code mode switch is hidden at this viewport (lg:hidden), so the preview badge is asserted directly rather than via a mode-switch click.
